description:
Poll an account-bootstrap session until the user completes verification. Uses exponential backoff (2s initial, 1.5x, 30s max) with jitter.

Agent usage: Call this after create_account with the returned session id. Terminal states: "verified" (this server keeps the session for this connection; the `user_id` field in the terminal body identifies the authenticated user), "expired", "completed_elsewhere" (email only: the user pressed "Sign in here" on the email link's page, so the browser they clicked from is signed in and this connection never will be — tell them so, and start a new login if this connection still needs one). A result with status "pending" means the wait ran out before the user finished — call this tool again with the same id. Works identically whether the underlying flow created a new User or logged in an existing one.

Before calling this for a challenge you created, make sure your reply text already shows the user what to act on — the link itself, the SMS text and number, or a note to check their inbox; a link that appeared only in a tool result is one they never saw.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wait time in seconds (default: 50, max: 600). Keep it under your MCP client's request timeout (the SDK default is 60 s) — a longer wait is cut off by the client while the server is still polling. On timeout the tool answers status "pending"; call it again with the same identifier.

name: wait_for_account_creation

last_status.description: On timeout: the last non-terminal status observed, or null when none was

message.description: On timeout: what to do next (call the tool again with the same identifier)

qr_code.description: Base64-encoded PNG QR code for the deep link

qr_text.description: UTF-8 text QR for terminal/agent rendering

status.description: "pending" when the wait ran out before a terminal state; otherwise the resource's own status

timeout_seconds.description: On timeout: the wait budget this call was given

type.description: Outcome of an account-session creation. `account_creation` means a new User will be written on verification. `login` indicates the submitted identity matched an existing User and the session will log them in.
